kpis.sub: MP CLOSED AT $39.57 ON OCT 30 (-5.0% THAT DAY), HOLDING NEAR ITS 52-WEEK LOW OF $37.11

Q3 results come Nov 5 after the close. USAR touched a new low of $8.89 before bouncing ~10% to ~$9.83 intraday on Oct 27; REMX closed $51.70 on Oct 26 (-28.4% total return over 12 months). kpis.sub: CHINA'S 12-MONTH SUSPENSION OF ITS OCT 2025 RARE-EARTH CONTROLS LAPSES IN 9 DAYS — NO RENEWAL CONFIRMED IN WHAT WE FOUND
kpis.label: The suspension of Beijing's October 2025 expanded controls expires Nov 10, 2026. Analysts frame three paths: extension, selective reinstatement, or full reimposition. April 2025 case-by-case licensing on seven elements (samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, yttrium) stays regardless. China mines ~69% of world rare earths and processes up to ~90%. No official extension announcement was found this week

themes.title: China's rare-earth suspension expires Nov 10 — extension, selective return or full reimposition all remain open
themes.description: The 12-month suspension of Beijing's October 2025 controls (the expanded element list and extraterritorial rules) ends Nov 10, nine days from now. We found no confirmed renewal this week. April 2025 licensing on seven elements remains in force either way. Western equities are already near 52-week lows, so markets are pricing a poor outcome rather than a resolved one — but a clean extension is not priced in as upside either.

themes.title: GM's termination of its VAC South Carolina magnet deal is still the key anchor-customer warning
themes.description: GM cancelled a 2023 supply agreement for e-VAC's ~$500M, ~2,000t/yr South Carolina plant (VAC has launched arbitration). Energy Fuels agreed in June to buy VAC for $1.9B and said the price may adjust with the arbitration. Western magnet capacity still needs anchor customers, not just policy; MP's Apple and DoD agreements are the contrast case.

themes.title: Juniors keep funding through equity and mergers while prices stay low
themes.description: Critical Metals' acquisition of European Lithium was approved by the WA Supreme Court on Oct 26 after the Oct 22 offering registration; Energy Fuels' $500M at-the-market programme continues to draw investor-rights probes with the stock at ~$7.56 near its $7.31 low. USAR's government money is milestone-based and its next earnings are estimated Nov 9.

themes.title: Lynas at a 52-week low into its September-quarter report — outcome not verified here

bear_case.title: The premium keeps deflating faster than the supply chain is built
bear_case.description: REMX closed $51.70 on Oct 26 (-28.4% total return over 12 months), MP is within ~7% of its 52-week low after a -5% day on Oct 30, USAR printed a new low at $8.89 and Lynas sat at A$10.71. MP remains loss-making at the EPS line on a high price-to-sales multiple, and the GM/VAC cancellation shows Western magnet capacity can lose anchor demand even with policy support.

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium carbonate has fallen ~25% in a month to CNY 93,600/t; Albemarle (~$99 after a 6% bounce) and Lithium Americas (~$2.05) reflect it. Copper holds ~$6.48/lb, but ~5% below its September record and with the AI-stock selloff a macro risk, Freeport (~$66) is exposed to an unwind even after a Q3 beat. A producer can be an excellent business at the wrong point in its price cycle.

bear_case.title: China can flood, freeze or consolidate
bear_case.description: The suspension of the October 2025 controls lapses Nov 10 with no confirmed renewal; April 2025 licensing remains. China holds ~69% of mine output and up to ~90% of processing, and a flood of cheap Chinese NdPr would undercut non-Chinese producers even with Pentagon price floors, which only protect projects that already have product. Lynas's NdPr output at ~70% of nameplate shows how depressed prices bite.

bear_case.title: Junior dilution, milestone funding and policy dependency
bear_case.description: Energy Fuels' $500M at-the-market programme, Critical Metals' offering registration and going-concern doubt, and USAR's milestone-only federal money show juniors funding through shares. Vault, EXIM and DoD floors are real but discretionary; no new Project Vault or EXIM developments were found this week.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Only US mine-to-magnet producer with Apple and DoD anchors and Q2 revenue up 89% to $108.5M, but at $39.57 (-5% on Oct 30, Goldman target cut to $57) with Q3 due Nov 5 and China's Nov 10 cliff ahead it is held as Core on business quality, not price. positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: Blacksburg construction and the Serra Verde deal are real, but a new 52-week low of $8.89 before a ~10% bounce to ~$9.83, milestone-based federal funding and China's export listing make this optionality with a genuine chance of zero.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: Thacker Pass is still the largest US lithium build, but at ~$2.05 (near its $2.02 low) with lithium carbonate down ~25% in a month to CNY 93.6k/t and mechanical completion not until late 2027, the size stays the smallest in the sleeve.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Excellent copper business with a Q3 beat (adj. EPS $0.88 vs $0.83) and 3.7B lb guided for 2027, but copper sits ~5% under its $6.85 record and the shares (~$66) trade with the macro tape, with the Section 232 tariff decision unresolved — a late-cycle price, not an entry point.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: Lithium carbonate fell a further 2.6% on Oct 30 to CNY 93.6k/t (-25% in a month); a 6% bounce to ~$99 off the $88.01 low is not a confirmed bottom, and Q3 on Nov 4 plus a new CEO in Feb 2027 leave the cycle question open.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths

positions.name: Energy Fuels

positions.name: Critical Metals
